images.description: Illustration of a Scout in a clean uniform with a compact red first-aid kit attached to their belt, standing confidently with arms relaxed at their sides, outdoors on a sunny day with trees and a trail in the background

Four-panel illustration showing different first aid settings: top-left a Scout treating a blister on a hiking trail in the woods, top-right a teenager helping someone who fell at home in a kitchen, bottom-left a sports sideline scene with an ice pack on an athlete's knee, bottom-right emergency responders helping people after a storm

A Scout pausing at the edge of an outdoor scene near a hiking trail, carefully scanning their surroundings for hazards before approaching an injured person who is sitting on the ground holding their knee, demonstrating scene safety evaluation

An infographic-style three-panel illustration showing the Check-Call-Care sequence: first panel shows a Scout looking around a park scene assessing for safety, second panel shows a Scout calmly speaking into a cell phone, third panel shows a Scout kneeling beside a seated person providing first aid with gloves on

A Scout calmly making a phone call while kneeling near an injured person lying in a park setting, with another Scout friend applying a bandage to the injured person's arm in the background, trees and a park bench visible

Two Scouts on a high mountain ridge, one holding up a cell phone trying to get a signal while the other studies a trail map, with dramatic mountain peaks and dense forest visible in the valley below, clear sky

Step-by-step illustration showing the correct pinch-and-peel technique for removing disposable nitrile gloves safely, with four sequential hand positions showing pinching the wrist, peeling off the first glove inside-out, tucking a finger under the second glove, and the final inside-out bundle ready for disposal
A Scout thoroughly washing their hands with soap and running water at an outdoor campsite wash station with a foot-pump water container, showing proper handwashing technique after providing first aid

A Scout carefully placing a person into the recovery position on a grassy field, the person lying on their side with top knee bent at a right angle for stability, head tilted slightly back, and the Scout adjusting their arm position

Close-up illustration showing the head-tilt chin-lift airway technique being performed on a CPR training mannequin, with one hand on the forehead tilting back and two fingers under the chin lifting upward, viewed from the side

A Scout wearing blue nitrile gloves performing a secondary assessment on a fellow Scout lying on the ground outdoors, carefully checking their forearm for injuries while the patient watches, first-aid kit open beside them

A Scout writing notes on a small spiral notepad while talking to a conscious patient who is sitting up against a tree trunk, both outdoors at a campsite, showing the SAMPLE history-gathering conversation

A Scout helping an injured person lie flat on their back on grass with their legs elevated on a backpack, covered with a light blanket, the Scout kneeling beside them looking attentive and calm, outdoor setting

An overhead view of a Scout camp activity area with three people who appear to need help at different spots, a Scout leader pointing and directing two other Scouts to assist, showing organized emergency triage response at a Scouting event

A Scout leader and a Scout sitting at a picnic table reviewing a health and medical record form together, with camping gear and a tent visible in the background, the Scout pointing at a section of the form

Close-up of a stainless steel medical alert bracelet on a Scout's wrist, showing the red medical caduceus symbol and small engraved text, with the Scout's clean uniform sleeve visible in the background

A neatly organized personal hiking first-aid kit spread out on a flat rock surface, with all items visible including bandages, gauze, gloves, tape, antiseptic wipes, tweezers, and a small red zippered carrying pouch beside them

A Scout and an adult leader standing at a camp table inspecting the contents of a large orange troop first-aid kit, the Scout holding up a package to check the expiration date while supplies are spread across the table

An educational illustration showing the three degrees of thermal burns side by side, with simplified cross-section diagrams of skin layers (epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous tissue) and visual indicators of superficial redness, partial-thickness blistering, and full-thickness damage
Three Scouts applying sunscreen to their arms and faces before a sunny outdoor activity, wearing hats and sunglasses, standing near a trailhead sign with bright sunshine and blue sky overhead

A Scout dressed in proper cold-weather layering system standing on a snowy trail, with labeled callout indicators pointing to the moisture-wicking base layer, insulating mid layer, and waterproof outer shell jacket
A Scout sitting on a trail-side rock carefully applying a moleskin patch to a hot spot on their heel, with one hiking boot and sock removed and placed beside them, backpack nearby on the trail

A close-up instructional illustration showing fine-tipped tweezers grasping a tick as close to the skin surface as possible, with an arrow indicating steady upward pulling motion, on a forearm with a small red mark around the tick

A Scout hiking carefully on a rocky trail wearing proper hiking boots and long pants, looking attentively at the trail ahead, with a small cautionary sign about snakes visible on a post beside the trail, desert Southwest landscape
A Scout wearing blue nitrile gloves carefully rinsing a small cut on another Scout's forearm under a stream of clean water poured from a camping water bottle, both Scouts outdoors at a campsite

A Scout carefully applying a large adhesive bandage to a cleaned scrape on a friend's knee, with the friend sitting on a camp bench and an open first-aid kit with visible supplies on the bench beside them

A Scout wearing gloves applying firm two-handed pressure with gauze to a simulated wound on another person's forearm during a first aid training exercise, with a first-aid kit and extra gauze pads visible nearby

A Scout demonstrating proper commercial tourniquet placement on a training leg model, showing the high-and-tight position on the upper thigh with the windlass rod visible, during a Stop the Bleed training session

A Scout demonstrating proper epinephrine auto-injector technique on a training device, pressing the orange tip firmly against the outer thigh, with another Scout watching and learning during a first aid class

Scouts resting at a high-altitude mountain campsite with dramatic peaks in the background, one Scout drinking from a water bottle while another checks on a teammate who is sitting on a rock and resting with their head in their hands
A Scout offering a small juice box to a fellow Scout who looks pale and slightly shaky, both sitting on a wooden bench at a campsite, a backpack and water bottles visible nearby

A Scout kneeling beside a person on the ground, carefully placing a folded jacket under their head for protection during a seizure, with camp chairs and gear moved away to clear the area around the person

A Scout standing on a wooden dock throwing a bright orange ring buoy with attached rope to a person in the water, demonstrating the throw step of reach-throw-row-go water rescue, lake and trees in background
A group of Scouts quickly moving as a group toward a sturdy building as dark storm clouds and a distant lightning bolt appear in the sky behind them, one Scout gesturing urgently for others to hurry

A Scout performing CPR chest compressions on a training mannequin on the floor, showing correct hand placement in the center of the chest with straight locked arms and shoulders positioned directly above the hands

An instructional illustration showing correct AED pad placement on an adult training mannequin chest, one pad on the upper right below the collarbone and one on the lower left side below the armpit, with a portable AED device visible beside the mannequin

An AED device in its bright green wall-mounted cabinet in a school hallway, with the universal heart and lightning bolt AED sign clearly visible above it, a window and lockers visible in the background showing a typical school setting

An educational diagram showing simplified side-by-side illustrations of musculoskeletal injuries: a strained muscle, a torn muscle, a ruptured tendon, a sprained ligament, a dislocated joint, a simple closed fracture, and a compound open fracture, each with labeled anatomical structures

A Scout carefully tying a triangular bandage arm sling on a fellow Scout, showing the correct finished position with the hand elevated slightly above the elbow, the knot tied at the side of the neck, both Scouts outdoors
A Scout applying a padded SAM splint to another Scout's forearm at a campsite, wrapping it securely with an elastic bandage, the patient sitting on a camp chair with the arm extended on a table

A Scout applying a folded triangular bandage around a fellow Scout's head, wrapping it carefully over a gauze pad and tying the knot at the side of the head away from the wound, both standing outdoors

Two Scouts practicing a low-crawl rescue drill in a training area, one Scout on hands and knees dragging another Scout by the clothing while staying close to the ground, simulating a smoke-filled room evacuation
A group of four Scouts constructing an improvised stretcher at a campsite, threading two sturdy wooden poles through the sleeves of buttoned-up jackets, with one Scout directing the process

An educational infographic showing the progression of heat illness from left to right: heat cramps with a person holding their calf muscle, heat exhaustion with a person sitting in shade looking pale and sweaty, and heat stroke with a person on the ground with someone calling for help, each stage labeled with key warning signs

Inside a camping tent, Scouts helping a fellow Scout who is wrapped in a sleeping bag, placing warm water bottles at the neck and armpits for rewarming, rain visible through the tent opening, a cup of warm drink nearby

A Scout standing at the top of a rappelling tower, eyes closed and taking a deep calming breath with hands at their sides, a safety harness and helmet visible, a belayer and supportive friends visible below giving encouragement

Two Scouts sitting together on a log at dusk near a campfire, one listening attentively and leaning in supportively while the other speaks, showing a caring and supportive peer conversation in a calm outdoor setting

An educational poster-style illustration showing the BE FAST stroke recognition steps: B for Balance showing a person losing balance, E for Eyes with blurred vision, F for Face with one side drooping, A for Arms with one arm drifting down, S for Speech with jumbled text, T for Time with a clock and phone showing 911

A Scout standing in front of a small semicircle of younger Scouts outdoors, demonstrating how to apply a triangular bandage arm sling on a volunteer, the learners watching attentively with some taking notes
Two Scouts practicing a first aid skill together outdoors, one Scout guiding the other through wrapping an elastic bandage around a wrist, representing the Guide phase of the EDGE teaching method

A four-panel collage showing different EMS career paths: an EMT standing beside an ambulance, a flight paramedic near a medical helicopter, an emergency physician in blue scrubs with a stethoscope, and a wilderness first responder with a medical pack on a mountain trail
A teen volunteer EMT in a clean dark blue EMS uniform standing proudly with arms crossed in front of a community ambulance station, an ambulance with emergency lights visible behind them

A Scout studying a Wilderness First Aid manual at an outdoor training course, sitting at a picnic table with CPR practice mannequins, bandaging supplies, and a SAM splint visible on the table, trees and a training facility in the background
